p: days was Hezekiah sick and near: Soon after that the Assyrians were slain: so that God will have the exercise of his children continually, that they may learn only to depend on God and aspire to the heavens.

turned his face toward the wall: For his heart was touched with fear of God's judgment, seeing he had appointed him to die so quickly after his deliverance from so great calamity, as one unworthy to remain in that estate, and also foreseeing the great change that would come in the Church, as he left no son to reign after him: for as yet Manasseh was not born, and when he reigned, we see what a tyrant he was.
from the hand of the king: He not only promises to prolong his life, but to give him rest and quietness from the Assyrians, who might have renewed their army to revenge their former defeat.
this shall be a sign to: For Hezekiah had asked for a sign for the confirmation of his faith, as in Isa 38:22, 2Ki 20:8, to which he was moved by the singular motion of God's spirit.
sun dial of Ahaz: Read 2Ki 20:8.

The writing of Hezekiah king of: He left this song of his lamentation and thanksgiving to all posterity, as a monument of his own infirmity and thankful heart for God's benefits, as David did, Ps 51:1.
At which time it was told to me, that I would die.

I shall not see the LORD: I will no more praise the Lord here in this temple among the faithful thus God permits his dearest children to want his consolation for a time that his grace afterward may appear when they feel their own weakness.
have cut off like a weaver: By my sin I have provoked God to take my life from me.
to night wilt thou make an: That is, in one day, or shortly.

till morning: Overnight I thought that I would live till morning, but my pangs in the night persuaded me the contrary: he shows the horror that the faithful have when they apprehend God's judgment against their sin.
chattered: I was so oppressed with sorrow, that I was not able to utter my words, but only to groan and sigh.
he hath both spoken to me: God has declared by his prophet that I will die and therefore I will yield to him.
softly all my years in the: I will have no release, but continual sorrows while I live.
by these things men live: They who will outlive the men that are now alive, and all they who are in these years will acknowledge this blessing.
restore me: That after that you had condemned me to death you restored me to life.
peace I had great bitterness: While I thought to have lived in rest and ease being delivered from my enemy, I had grief upon grief.
sins behind thy back: He values more the remission of his sins, and God's favour than a thousand lives.

the grave cannot praise thee: For as much as God has placed man in this world to glorify him, the godly take it as a sign of his wrath, when their days were shortened, either because they seemed unworthy for their sins to live longer in his service, or for their zeal to God's glory, seeing that there are so few in earth who regard it as in Ps 6:5,115:17.
children shall make known thy truth: All posterity will acknowledge and the fathers according to their duty toward their children will instruct them in your graces and mercies toward me.
our life in the house of: He shows what is the use of the Congregation and Church, that is, to give the Lord thanks for his benefits.
lay it for a plaster upon: Read 2Ki 20:7.
had said: As in Isa 38:7.
